prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active peptide forms of glucagon-like peptide-1 that made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After reading the full first-round exchange I keep a single prize part on B019 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case has not weakened: the arc from gut-hormone physiology (Holst) through proglucagon-peptide biology and its translational program (Drucker) to identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov) is complete, replicated for decades, and now confirmed in large independent randomized trials in type 2 diabetes and obesity with emerging cardiovascular and renal signals. Round 1 produced no argument that the science is immature or that a second prize part would help. The remaining disagreement is about attribution, not merit, and I do not think a disputed third place is the same as a doubtful discovery. I would word the citation around the peptide and its physiology, so that it neither claims liraglutide or semaglutide nor implies they were unimportant.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness is real and I cannot remove it from the material in front of me. The Mojsov versus Habener-group priority question rests on recollection, not on documents I can check, and Habener is not among the credited names. Excluding Lotte Bjerre Knudsen leaves the medicinal chemistry that produced the drugs unrecognised, and a citation built on discovery may be read as favouring academic over industrial work. Long-term safety and durability of weight loss are still being defined. B002 is a cleaner two-person credit with conceptual originality, and if the Mojsov question were shown to be materially weaker than recalled, B002 would become the stronger configuration for me.

responses.point: You would test the Mojsov inclusion more closely and, if the Habener priority dispute proved unresolvable, would rather weigh Knudsen openly for the third place than keep Mojsov by default.
responses.response: I agree the inclusion should be tested, and I answer the chair's documentary question with a limit: I cannot establish first biological activity or first synthesis from the supplied record, and I will not pretend recollection is evidence. Where I differ is on the fallback. Swapping Knudsen in for Mojsov would change the citation from discovery to development, and the physiology trio would lose the step that connects incretin biology to a therapeutic peptide. If Mojsov's priority proved clearly worse than recalled, I would move to B002 before I would rebuild B019 around a development credit. If the dispute is only unresolved, not decided against her, I would hold the trio and record the dispute openly.

responses.point: You moved B019 to the top of your configuration after opening with the unfolded protein response, while keeping B002 as your first alternative and noting that its limited clinical translation matters less for a basic-mechanism prize.
responses.response: Your last point is the strongest argument for B002 and I accept it: clinical translation of the unfolded protein response is early, but that is not a defect in a prize for a mechanism. The question is therefore which discovery has the larger completed case today, and I still judge that to be B019, because its mechanism, human physiology and outcome evidence are all confirmed. I do not treat B002's compact Walter and Mori credit as a small advantage; it is the reason B002 is my first fallback and should be next in line, not an afterthought. Your uncertainty about mammalian PERK and ATF6 contributions does not weaken the Mori and Walter pair enough to change that.

responses.point: You would move to B002 without hesitation if the committee judged the GLP-1 credit unsettled, and you asked what level of unsettled credit would count.
responses.response: I would set the threshold at the Mojsov place, not at B019 as a whole. Holst and Drucker are not disputed in any round-1 file, so uncertainty over a single seat should lead us to examine that seat, and to move to B002 only if the evidence shows the identification and synthesis of the active peptide cannot be credited to her in good faith. A difference of emphasis with the Habener group would not meet that threshold for me. I also agree with you that splitting B019 would not solve the Knudsen problem under the three-person cap, and that you are right to keep that exclusion as a stated cost in our reasoning.

responses.point: You asked whether B002 can wait without loss while B019 attribution is checked, and whether Miesenbock or Nagel belongs in an optogenetics trio.
responses.response: I do not support deferring B019 for sequencing. Nothing in the round-1 files suggests the GLP-1 case will look weaker next year, and deferral would turn an unresolved but bounded credit question into a reason to delay the discovery with the most complete evidence. B002 can be recognised later without losing its case, since its credit is compact and its mechanism is settled, but that argues for patience on B002, not for postponing B019. On optogenetics I keep Nagel over Miesenbock in any trio, for the reasons Perlmann gave, and I still see B004 as the least ready of the three leading candidates because any three of six names leaves a visible omission.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 form can be credited ahead of the Habener group; I cannot verify this from the supplied material.
Whether the committee can state the exclusion of Knudsen openly without implying that drug development was unimportant.
Long-term safety, durability of weight loss and the full cardiovascular and renal evidence are still accumulating.
Whether the mammalian PERK and ATF6 work affects the compact Walter and Mori credit for B002, which would matter if I had to fall back.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my first-round disclosure. My profile lists co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and a shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation, and I note that Linnarsson is a member of this committee. None of them is a credited name on B019, B002 or B004, and my single-cell RNA-sequencing work does not bear on any shortlisted ballot. I request no recusal.
